questions.question_text: A Wyoming salesperson posts a property listing on social media using only her personal name. What violation has occurred?
questions.correct_answer: A blind ad without broker identification
distractors: Failure to obtain a social media license
questions.explanation: A salesperson may not advertise real estate without including the real estate company name under which they are licensed, and the rule reaches every ad "displayed digitally or in print," social media included (W.S. 33-28-119(g); WREC Rules ch. 6 § 4). A post carrying only a personal name is a blind ad.

questions.question_text: A licensee creates an online listing for a vacant lot but never obtained the owner's permission. Which rule was violated?
distractors: Failing to include the property address
Listing vacant land without a survey
questions.explanation: Offering real estate for sale or lease "without the knowledge and consent of the owner or his authorized agent, or on terms other than those authorized by the owner" is a ground for discipline (W.S. 33-28-111(a)(viii)), and that reaches print, internet, and social media alike. A separate ground requires the owner's written consent before placing a sign.

questions.question_text: Which name must appear in all Wyoming real estate advertisements?
questions.correct_answer: The real estate company name as licensed by the Commission
distractors: A registered trade name or team name by itself
questions.explanation: Every advertisement must include the real estate company name under which the licensee is licensed, and that name must appear conspicuously and concurrently with any registered trade, group, or team name (W.S. 33-28-119(f), (g); WREC Rules ch. 6 § 4(a)). A trade or team name alone is not enough. Wyoming does not require a license number in advertising.

questions.question_text: A broker uses a catchy slogan as the only identifier on a billboard promoting residential listings. Is this compliant with Wyoming advertising rules?
questions.correct_answer: No, the licensed real estate company name is required
distractors: Yes, slogans satisfy the identification rule
Yes, if the broker's phone number is included
No, billboards are prohibited for licensees
questions.explanation: A licensee promoting real estate activities must use the real estate company name under which they are licensed, and may use no slogan suggesting the property is offered by an unlicensed private party (W.S. 33-28-119(a)). Billboards are expressly covered as an advertising medium, so a slogan by itself leaves the ad blind.

questions.question_text: A WREC investigator reviews a brokerage's Instagram account and finds posts listing homes with only the salesperson's photo and phone number. What enforcement action is most likely?
questions.correct_answer: An administrative fine and/or censure for the advertising violation
distractors: Immediate license revocation of the agent
A warning with no further action required
questions.explanation: Social media posts must carry the licensed real estate company name; posts showing only a salesperson's photo and phone number are blind ads (W.S. 33-28-119(g); WREC Rules ch. 6 § 4). For a first advertising violation the Commission's likely response is an administrative fine of up to $2,500 per offense, censure, or both, not revocation.

questions.question_text: A salesperson leaves Broker A to join Broker B. Under Wyoming law, who must notify the Real Estate Commission?
questions.correct_answer: The salesperson, and Broker A upon the termination
distractors: Both Broker A and Broker B, but not the salesperson
questions.explanation: The duty is split: the former responsible broker must immediately notify the Commission for cancellation of the license upon termination, and the licensee must notify the Commission promptly in writing and pay the fee (W.S. 33-28-109(c)). The new broker has no notification duty; they sign the transfer form certifying active supervision.

questions.question_text: A salesperson is terminated by her broker on March 1 but does not affiliate with a new broker. What is the status of her license?
questions.correct_answer: She cannot practice; the license is held, then goes inactive
distractors: It remains active for 90 days after termination
It converts to a broker license
questions.explanation: A returned license may be held on a "hold for transfer" basis for not more than 30 days, after which it automatically becomes inactive (WREC Rules ch. 1 § 5). While the license is returned, on hold, or inactive the licensee "shall not perform any real estate activity."

questions.question_text: A brokerage opens a second office location in Sheridan. What must the broker do regarding WREC?
questions.correct_answer: Register the branch office with WREC
distractors: Hire a branch manager with 5 years experience
File a new business entity application
questions.explanation: A company license is issued to the responsible broker for each branch office maintained, and the broker must submit a branch office application plus a plan of supervision for Commission approval (W.S. 33-28-109(b)). The branch stays under the responsible broker's supervision, so no separate broker license or independently qualified branch manager is required.

questions.question_text: A salesperson whose license is inactive due to broker termination shows a property to a buyer. What is the consequence?
distractors: No violation if a sale is not completed
questions.explanation: A licensee on inactive status may not engage in any real estate activity, and "participating in real estate activity while a license is on inactive status" is an express ground for discipline (WREC Rules ch. 1 § 5(e), ch. 6 § 1(a)(ii)). Showing a property is real estate activity, and the 30-day hold period permits no practice either.

questions.question_text: Broker A terminates a salesperson but fails to notify WREC. Meanwhile, the salesperson closes a transaction under Broker B. Who bears regulatory liability?
questions.correct_answer: Both brokers may face WREC discipline
distractors: Only Broker A for failing to notify
No liability if the transaction was proper
questions.explanation: Broker A violated the duty to immediately notify the Commission for cancellation on termination (W.S. 33-28-109(c)). Broker B has no notification duty, but failing to supervise an affiliated licensee is its own ground for discipline (33-28-111(a)(ix)). WREC may act against a licensee and that licensee's responsible broker alike, so both are exposed.

questions.question_text: In Wyoming, who is ultimately accountable for the real estate activities of affiliated licensees?
questions.explanation: Wyoming law makes the responsible broker accountable for all real estate activities conducted by affiliated licensees. This includes ensuring compliance with WREC rules, maintaining trust accounts, and keeping proper transaction records.

questions.question_text: A salesperson mishandles earnest money by depositing it into a personal account. Besides the salesperson, who else may face discipline?
questions.explanation: The responsible broker is accountable for trust account management and all real estate activities of affiliated licensees. Even if the salesperson acted independently, the broker's supervisory duty makes them subject to WREC discipline for the trust fund violation.

questions.question_text: Which records must a Wyoming responsible broker maintain for WREC examination?
questions.explanation: Wyoming's responsible broker must maintain trust accounts and transaction records and make them available for WREC examination upon request. This recordkeeping requirement supports consumer protection and regulatory oversight of brokerage operations.

questions.question_text: A responsible broker discovers that an affiliated salesperson has been practicing outside the scope of the License Act. What is the broker's obligation?
questions.correct_answer: Take corrective action and ensure compliance
distractors: Wait for WREC to investigate first
Report only if a complaint is filed
questions.explanation: The responsible broker must ensure all affiliated licensees comply with WREC rules and the License Act. Upon discovering a violation, the broker has an affirmative duty to take immediate corrective action rather than waiting for a formal complaint or investigation.

questions.question_text: A brokerage has 15 salespersons and no written supervision policies. During an audit, WREC finds multiple compliance failures across the office. How will WREC likely view the broker's role?
distractors: WREC has no authority over internal policies
The broker is exempt if no complaints existed
questions.explanation: The responsible broker is the individual responsible for supervising the licensees associated with the company, and failure to supervise is an express ground for discipline (W.S. 33-28-102(b)(xlix), 33-28-111(a)(ix)). Widespread compliance failures across a 15-agent office point squarely at inadequate oversight. A written supervision plan is required only for branch offices, but its absence is strong evidence the duty was unmet.
